profiles.name: Figma
profiles.why: Figma's own homepage lists "Wireframes" as just one of many community template categories within a broader high-fidelity design-to-build canvas (https://www.figma.com), while Balsamiq is purpose-built around wireframing, sizing its monthly AI credits per editor explicitly to wireframe and prototype counts (E17) and offering an MCP server so wireframes can be read, edited, and built on directly from Claude or Cursor (E4). This suggests a buyer already in Figma for high-fidelity work might still choose a dedicated wireframing tool with AI-assistant integration for the earlier, lower-fidelity stage, rather than evidence that Figma cannot be used for wireframes.
profiles.discovery_reason: The buyer's team often already works in Figma for high-fidelity design and wonders whether wireframing should just happen there too instead of adding a separate tool.
profiles.promise: Teammates and AI agents work together on one AI-native canvas, from first idea through to shipped product.
profiles.pricing: Not published on these pages in figures; Figma Weave states it is free to start with advanced features and higher usage on paid plans, no price amounts given.
profiles.free_entry: Get started / signup link on homepage with no stated conditions; Figma Weave explicitly offers a free starting tier before paid plans.
profiles.icp: Creative teams and professional creatives who need to generate, edit, and scale visual assets, and whole product teams going 'from WIP to ship, together.'
